newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PSG LEAD QUALITY FOURSOME INTO CUP SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG LEAD QUALITY FOURSOME INTO CUP SEMIS.

text.p: Four clubs of the highest pedigree qualified for the semifinals of the European Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday - with defending champion Paris St Germain leading the way.

Patrice Loko hit a hat-trick as the French side beat AEK 3-0 in Athens to banish memories of their goalless first leg while three-times winners Barcelona went through 4-2 on aggregate after drawing 1-1 at AIK Stockholm.

Joining them in the last four are Italy's Fiorentina, who beat Benfica of Portugal 2-1 on aggregate despite losing 1-0 at home on Thursday, and Liverpool, who overcame Norwegian outsiders Brann Bergen 3-0 for a 4-1 aggregate.
Loko scored twice in the first half and once late on to send PSG into their fifth successive European semifinal.

The French side had been lacklustre in the first leg but came out firing on all cylinders as Loko's goals in the 22nd and 43rd minutes left the Greeks facing a mountain they never looked capable of climbing. He completed his hat-trick 10 minutes from time.

Barcelona, leading 3-1 from the first leg, effectively finished their tie after just 12 minutes in Stockholm as Brazilian striker Ronaldo converted a Hristo Stoichkov cross to secure a vital away goal.
Pascal Simpson earned AIK a creditable 1-1 draw on the night when he scored in the 75th minute but Barca, winners of the trophy in 1979, 1982 and 1989, were never in real danger.
Thousands of Fiorentina fans stayed silent throughout the first half in Florence in protest at the banning of 27 supporters following the stoning of the Juventus team bus before a recent league game.
Maybe lacking inspiration, Fiorentina's defence was in disarray as they left Benfica's Edgar Pacheco unmarked to score from close range in the 22nd minute.
After the break the silence was replaced by a cauldron of noise and smoke, but it wasn't enough to force a goal from the home side, although Francesco Baiano hit a post.
Fiorentina, the first winners of this competition back in 1961, survived some tense moments but held out to go into Friday's semifinal draw.
Liverpool, the only one of the semifinalists never to have won the trophy, started cautiously before eventually overwhelming Brann.
Robbie Fowler settled the Anfield nerves when he scored with a penalty in the 25th minute after he had been felled in the area.
Patrick Berger missed three straightforward chances and paid the price by being substituted by Stan Collymore after an hour.
It took Collymore just two minutes to announce his presence as he bustled through two tackles to make it 2-0.

Liverpool, four times European champions and twice UEFA Cup winners are seeking to join Barcelona, Juventus, Ajax and Bayern Munich as the only teams to have won all three European trophies, and made it 3-0 with Fowler's second 12 minutes from time.
